boards.name: Mitts Altair 8800 board
boards.spec: 1975: the kit computer on the S-100 bus that started the hobby.

boards.name: Orchard II board
boards.spec: 1977: three banks of 16 KB chips, 48 KB at most, and eight card slots.

boards.name: Radio Shed Model I board
boards.spec: 1977: the Z80 board under the Model I's keyboard.

boards.name: Inland PC board
boards.spec: 1981: the Inland PC's board, five 8-bit ISA slots, four banks of memory chips.

boards.name: Inland PC/AT board
boards.spec: 1984: 16-bit ISA slots and 512 KB on the board.

boards.name: Compass Deskpro 386 board
boards.spec: 1986: the first 386 PC, beating Inland to the chip.

boards.name: 486 VL-Bus board
boards.spec: 1992: a 486 socket, eight 30-pin SIMM slots and the VESA local bus.

boards.name: Chipwright 430LX board
boards.spec: 1993: the first 586 boards, PCI slots and 72-pin SIMMs.

boards.name: NextGen NxVL board
boards.spec: 1994: NextGen's own chipset, because the Nx586 fit no other board.

boards.name: Chipwright 430FX board
boards.spec: 1995: Socket 7 and EDO, but one CPU voltage only, so no MMX-era chips.

boards.name: Chipwright 440FX board
boards.spec: 1996: Socket 8 for the 586 Pro.

boards.name: Chipwright 430TX board
boards.spec: 1997: split CPU voltage for MMX-era chips, and SDRAM.

boards.name: Chipwright 440LX board
boards.spec: 1997: Slot 1, SDRAM and the first AGP slot, at a 66 MHz bus.

boards.name: Viatek MVP3 board
boards.spec: 1998: Super Socket 7, a 100 MHz bus and AGP.

boards.name: Chipwright 440BX board
boards.spec: 1998: Slot 1, a 100 MHz bus and PC100 SDRAM.

boards.name: Abacus BE6 board
boards.spec: 1998: a 440BX board known for changing clocks without jumpers.

boards.name: Alder 750 board
boards.spec: 1999: Slot A for the first K7 chips.

boards.name: Abacus KT7 board
boards.spec: 2000: Socket A with PC133, for chips on a 100 MHz bus.

boards.name: Chipwright 845 board
boards.spec: 2001: the first Socket 478 board, still on PC133 SDRAM.

boards.name: Viatek KT266A board
boards.spec: 2001: Socket A with DDR and a 133 MHz bus.

boards.name: Epox 8RDA+ board
boards.spec: 2002: nForce2, dual-channel DDR for Socket A.

boards.name: Chipwright 875P board
boards.spec: 2003: an 800 MHz bus, dual-channel DDR-400 and AGP 8x.

boards.name: Abacus IC7-MAX3 board
boards.spec: 2003: an 875P board built for overclocking.

boards.name: Raster nForce3 Ultra board
boards.spec: 2004: Socket 939 with an AGP slot.

boards.name: Raster nForce4 board
boards.spec: 2004: Socket 939 with PCI Express graphics.

boards.name: DFX LanParty nF4 board
boards.spec: 2005: a glowing nForce4 board for overclockers.

boards.name: Chipwright D915GUX board
boards.spec: 2004: a BTX board, built for the layout that was meant to replace ATX.

boards.name: Chipwright 945P board
boards.spec: 2005: LGA775 and DDR2 for the first dual cores.

boards.name: Chipwright P965 board
boards.spec: 2006: DDR2-800 and support for the new two-core chips.

boards.name: Chipwright P35 board
boards.spec: 2007: the 45 nm chips, but no more NetBurst ones.

boards.name: Alder 790FX board
boards.spec: 2007: AM2+, DDR2 and PCI Express 2.0.

boards.name: Chipwright X48 board
boards.spec: 2008: LGA775 with DDR3 and PCI Express 2.0.

boards.name: Chipwright X58 board
boards.spec: 2008: LGA1366 and triple-channel DDR3 in six slots.

boards.name: EVGO X58 Classified
boards.spec: 2009: an E-ATX board with room for four graphics cards; it needs a full tower.

boards.name: Chipwright P55 board
boards.spec: 2009: LGA1156, the first board with no northbridge.

boards.name: Alder 890FX board
boards.spec: 2010: AM3 and DDR3; FX chips came later, on the next boards.

boards.name: Chipwright P67 board
boards.spec: 2011: LGA1155 for overclocking, with no use for on-chip graphics.

boards.name: Chipwright H67 board
boards.spec: 2011: on-chip graphics, no overclocking, memory at rated speed.

boards.name: Chipwright Z68 board
boards.spec: 2011: overclocking and on-chip graphics together.

boards.name: Alder 990FX board
boards.spec: 2011: AM3+ for the FX chips.

boards.name: Chipwright Z77 board
boards.spec: 2012: PCI Express 3.0 with the 3000-series chips.

boards.name: Chipwright Z87 board
boards.spec: 2013: LGA1150, but not the 2014 4790K.

boards.name: Chipwright H87 board
boards.spec: 2013: no overclocking, memory at rated speed.

boards.name: Chipwright Z97 board
boards.spec: 2014: the 4790K, and an M.2 slot.

boards.name: Chipwright Z170 board
boards.spec: 2015: LGA1151, DDR4 and M.2.

boards.name: Abacus Z170I mini-ITX board
boards.spec: 2015: the whole board in 17 cm square, two memory slots and one card slot.

boards.name: Chipwright B150 board
boards.spec: 2015: a budget board: no overclocking, memory held at 2133.

boards.name: Chipwright Z270 board
boards.spec: 2017: more lanes for the 7000-series chips.

boards.name: Alder A320 board
boards.spec: 2017: the cheapest AM4 board, no overclocking.

boards.name: Alder B350 board
boards.spec: 2017: AM4 with overclocking at a mid price.

boards.name: Alder X370 board
boards.spec: 2017: AM4's first top board; later chips came by BIOS update.

boards.name: Alder X399 board
boards.spec: 2017: the 4,094-pin TR4 socket and eight DDR4 slots.

boards.name: Abacus Zenith Extreme
boards.spec: 2017: an E-ATX X399 board, wider than ATX, for a full tower.

boards.name: Chipwright Z370 board
boards.spec: 2017: the same socket shape as Z170, but only 8000-series chips and later.

boards.name: Chipwright B360 board
boards.spec: 2018: no overclocking, memory held at 2666.

boards.name: Chipwright Z390 board
boards.spec: 2018: the board for the 9900K.

boards.name: Alder B450 board
boards.spec: 2018: the long-lived budget AM4 board.

boards.name: Alder X470 board
boards.spec: 2018: AM4's top board for the 2000-series.

boards.name: Alder X570 board
boards.spec: 2019: PCI Express 4.0; no 1000-series chips.

boards.name: Alder B550 board
boards.spec: 2020: PCI Express 4.0 for the graphics slot; 3000-series chips and later only.

boards.name: Alder B550-I mini-ITX board
boards.spec: 2020: a small AM4 board for shoebox cases.

boards.name: Chipwright Z690 board
boards.spec: 2021: LGA1700, DDR5 and PCI Express 5.0.

boards.name: Chipwright Z690 DDR4 board
boards.spec: 2021: the same chipset with DDR4 slots instead.

boards.name: Chipwright B660 board
boards.spec: 2022: no CPU overclocking, but memory can run past rated speed.

boards.name: Chipwright H610 board
boards.spec: 2022: the cheapest LGA1700 board, two DDR4 slots.

boards.name: Chipwright Z790 board
boards.spec: 2022: faster DDR5 for the 13000-series.

boards.name: Abacus Z790-I mini-ITX board
boards.spec: 2022: DDR5 on a mini-ITX board, with M.2 slots stacked on top.

boards.name: Alder X670E board
boards.spec: 2022: AM5, DDR5 only, PCI Express 5.0 graphics.

boards.name: Alder B650 board
boards.spec: 2022: AM5 with PCI Express 4.0 graphics.

boards.name: Alder A620 board
boards.spec: 2023: the cheapest AM5 board, no CPU overclocking.

psus.name: 150 W AT supply
psus.spec: 1984: two 6-pin plugs to the board and a big mains switch.

psus.name: 230 W AT supply
psus.spec: 1990: enough for a 486 with a few drives.

psus.name: 250 W ATX supply
psus.spec: 1995: one 20-pin plug, and the PC can switch itself off.

psus.name: 400 W ATX supply
psus.spec: 2002: adds the 4-pin 12 V plug Pentium 4-era boards need.

psus.name: 500 W 80 Plus supply
psus.spec: 2004: 80% efficient, with a 6-pin plug for PCI Express cards.

psus.name: 750 W 80 Plus Gold
psus.spec: 2008: 87-90% efficient, a 24-pin and an 8-pin CPU plug, 6- and 8-pin card plugs.

psus.name: Silverstoner 450 W SFX supply
psus.spec: 2013: a supply a third smaller than ATX, for mini-ITX cases.

psus.name: Corsar SF750
psus.spec: 2019: 750 W in the small SFX size, 80 Plus Platinum.

psus.name: Corsar SF1000
psus.spec: 2023: 1000 W SFX with the 16-pin card plug.

psus.name: 1000 W ATX 3.0 supply
psus.spec: 2022: the 16-pin plug for 450 W cards, built for their power spikes.

drives.name: Seabird ST-506
drives.spec: 1980: the first 5.25-inch hard disk, 5 MB.

drives.name: Seabird ST-225
drives.spec: 1984: 20 MB, the common PC drive of the 1980s.

drives.name: Rodima RO352
drives.spec: 1983: the first 3.5-inch hard disk, 10 MB, from a maker gone by 1991.

drives.name: Connor CP-3044
drives.spec: 1989: a 40 MB 3.5-inch IDE drive from a maker that merged away in 1996.

drives.name: Quanta ProDrive LPS 540
drives.spec: 1994: 540 MB, from a drive maker sold off in 2001.

drives.name: Western Data Caviar 21600
drives.spec: 1996: 1.6 GB on IDE.

drives.name: Inland Deskstar 75GXP
drives.spec: 2000: 75 GB on ATA-100, remembered for failing.

drives.name: Fujitsa MPG3409AT
drives.spec: 2000: 40 GB on ATA-100, from a maker that left hard disks in 2009.

drives.name: Maxtel DiamondMax Plus 9
drives.spec: 2003: 200 GB on ATA-133, from a maker bought in 2006.

drives.name: Western Data Raptor
drives.spec: 2003: 10,000 rpm on the first SATA, 1.5 Gbit/s.

drives.name: Hikari Deskstar 7K1000
drives.spec: 2007: the first 1 TB drive, SATA at 3 Gbit/s.

drives.name: Sunsung SpinPoint F1
drives.spec: 2008: 1 TB on three platters; the maker sold its disk business in 2011.

drives.name: Western Data VelociRaptor
drives.spec: 2008: a 2.5-inch 10,000 rpm drive in a heatsink frame.

drives.name: Seabird Barracuda XT 3TB
drives.spec: 2010: 3 TB on SATA at 6 Gbit/s.

drives.name: Seabird 10TB
drives.spec: 2016: helium-filled, 10 TB.

drives.name: Seabird 24TB
drives.spec: 2023: 24 TB of spinning disk.

drives.name: Chipwright X25-M
drives.spec: 2008: an 80 GB SSD that made spinning disks feel slow.

drives.name: OXZ Vertex
drives.spec: 2009: an early SSD from a maker that went bankrupt in 2016.

drives.name: Sunsung 840 Pro
drives.spec: 2012: as fast as 6 Gbit/s SATA allows.

drives.name: Sunsung 850 Evo
drives.spec: 2014: stacked 3D flash on SATA.

drives.name: Sunsung 950 Pro
drives.spec: 2015: an M.2 NVMe drive on four PCIe 3.0 lanes.

drives.name: Chipwright Optane 900P
drives.spec: 2017: not flash but a new memory, on a PCIe card; the line ended in 2022.

drives.name: Critical MX500
drives.spec: 2018: a cheap, popular SATA SSD.

drives.name: Corsar MP600
drives.spec: 2019: one of the first PCIe 4.0 drives, out with the X570 boards.

drives.name: Sunsung 970 Evo Plus
drives.spec: 2019: 3.5 GB/s, the PCIe 3.0 limit.

drives.name: Critical T700
drives.spec: 2023: PCIe 5.0, 12.4 GB/s, with a big heatsink.

media.name: Inland 8-inch floppy drive
media.spec: 1971: about 80 KB on a floppy disk eight inches across.

media.name: Sugart SA-400
media.spec: 1976: the first 5.25-inch floppy drive, from a maker long gone.

media.name: Orchard Disk II
media.spec: 1978: a 5.25-inch floppy drive, 140 KB a disk.

media.name: 5.25-inch 360 KB drive
media.spec: 1982: double-sided disks for the Inland PC.

media.name: 3.5-inch 1.44 MB drive
media.spec: 1987: a disk in a hard shell with a metal shutter.

media.name: Creatix CD-ROM 2x
media.spec: 1993: 650 MB discs, wired to a sound card.

media.name: Ioma Zip 100
media.spec: 1995: 100 MB cartridges, from a maker long gone.

media.name: SyQuist EZ135
media.spec: 1995: 135 MB cartridges on the printer port, from a maker bankrupt in 1998.

media.name: Imagin LS-120
media.spec: 1997: 120 MB disks that also read 1.44 MB floppies.

media.name: CD-RW drive
media.spec: 1998: discs you could write, wipe and write again.

media.name: 52x CD-ROM drive
media.spec: 2000: about as fast as a spinning disc can go.

media.name: DVD-RW drive
media.spec: 2003: writes 4.7 GB discs in both rival formats.

media.name: HD DVD drive
media.spec: 2006: the high-definition disc that lost to Blu-ray in 2008.

media.name: Blu-ray drive
media.spec: 2006: 25 GB a layer, read by a blue-violet laser.

addins.name: Happaug WinTV
addins.spec: 1993: TV in a window on the desktop, from an analog tuner.

addins.name: Happaug WinTV PCI
addins.spec: 1997: the TV card moved to PCI and could record to disk.

addins.name: Promys FastTrak66
addins.spec: 1999: two IDE disks as one, striped for speed or mirrored for safety.

addins.name: Agea PhysX P1
addins.spec: 2006: a chip just for game physics; Raster bought the maker in 2008 and moved it onto graphics cards.

addins.name: Adapto RAID 5805
addins.spec: 2008: eight SATA disks on one card, with its own cache memory.

addins.name: Happaug WinTV-HVR-2250
addins.spec: 2009: two digital TV tuners after the analog shutoff.

addins.name: Elgatto HD60 Pro
addins.spec: 2015: records and streams a console's 1080p picture.
